lecture_context.lecture_title: What’s Going On Inside My Model?

unit.name: Capability benchmarks, contamination, and safety dashboards
unit.description: Covers benchmark-based capability evaluation, benchmark contamination checks, and safety/agentic-workflow evaluation dashboards for release and RLHF decisions.
unit.summary: Capability dashboards evaluate model checkpoints across tasks such as reasoning, coding, math, and multilingual performance, and they can expose clusters of errors in a specific checkpoint [ts=5125s] [ts=5161s]. The lecture warns that public benchmarks can be contaminated when test examples or related explanations appear in training data, so benchmark numbers are more useful comparatively than as absolute truth [ts=5211s] [ts=5270s]. Detection methods include n-gram searches, hashes, and semantic embedding searches between test and training examples, followed by removing exposed examples and replacing them with held-out offline ones [ts=5321s] [ts=5343s] [ts=5367s] [ts=5391s]. Safety evaluations stress-test models for jailbreaks, social engineering, misuse, harmful content, hallucinations, privacy leakage, and behavior inside agentic workflows; these dashboards help release decisions and target expensive SFT/RLHF work to failing areas [ts=5412s] [ts=5440s] [ts=5500s].

key_points.text: Capability benchmarks evaluate model skills such as reasoning, coding, math, multilingual tasks, and instruction following across checkpoints.
Error clusters can show that one checkpoint regressed on a particular capability such as reasoning.
Benchmark contamination occurs when held-out test content or close variants appear in the training data.
Contamination can be detected with n-gram search, hashes, or embedding-based semantic search.
When a test set is exposed, the suggested response is to remove exposed examples and replace them with newly held-out offline items.
Safety evaluations include jailbreaks, social engineering, misuse, harmful content, hallucination, privacy leakage, and agentic-workflow behavior.
Evaluation dashboards can inform go/no-go release decisions and focus RLHF on the evals that are actually failing.
